# Dock tab headers admit only the close action — host-authored header actions cannot be projected or routed

A Dock host cannot put its own actions into a projected tab header. The tab subsystem supports it —
`tab.Container#headerActions` is a public reactive config, and #17874 makes focus gating a general
`showOnFocus` — but the Dock's projection owns that slot and admits exactly one action.

## Three gaps, all in the projection

| # | site | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `dashboard/dock/projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs:942` | builds `headerActions` **only** from `enableDockCloseAction`; no option carries additional actions |
| 2 | `dashboard/dock/projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs:1012` | the `headerAction` listener forwards only `data.action === 'close'`; every other intent is swallowed |
| 3 | `dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:1505` | `onDockHeaderAction` is wired *inside* the `enableDockCloseAction` spread, so a host wanting custom actions without the close action gets no handler at all |

Gap 2 is the one that makes a workaround impossible: even if a host got an action rendered, pressing
it would reach nothing.

## What already works, and should not be rebuilt

- `enableDockCloseAction` projects a persistent close action, routes it through the model as
  `closeItem` on the resolved active item, owns focus succession, and keeps `hidden` synchronised
  against each item's `closable` policy. A host wanting only "an always-visible close button that
  closes the active tab" needs **no new engine code** — just the flag.
- Focus gating is generic after #17874: an action carrying `showOnFocus: true` (the tab header
  default) is exposed while its TabContainer holds focus. No Dock-specific gating is needed.

So this ticket is only about **admitting host-authored actions into the projection and routing their
intent back out**.

## Shape

`getDockProjectionOptions()` is the documented host hook ("the default contributes nothing"), so the
option should arrive through it and be threaded into `LayoutAdapter.project`. Per-tabs-node
resolution matters: a host will want different actions on different zones, so an array alone is
likely too weak — a resolver receiving the node id is the shape to weigh against it.

Intent should travel the existing `onDockHeaderAction` seam rather than a parallel callback; the
Workspace already returns `null` for actions it does not own, so forwarding everything is safe and
keeps one path.

## Contract Ledger

Added 2026-08-30 at reviewer request (PR #17879 RA-1). This is the consumed surface the
implementation is held to; the PR reconciles against these rows.

### `resolveDockHeaderActions` — the host resolver

| aspect | contract |
|---|---|
| supplied via | `DockWorkspace#getDockProjectionOptions()`, the documented host hook. Absent ⇒ projection byte-identical to before this feature. |
| signature | `(nodeId: String) => Object[] \| null \| undefined` |
| **why `nodeId` alone** | The active item is deliberately **not** passed. A resolver that could see it would be invited to return a per-item action LIST, and a list that changes between projections replaces the action group — destroying the stable instances `actionVisibilityChange` consumers such as tab Overflow bind to. Per-item behaviour belongs on the instance. |
| return | Action configs in the shape `toolbar.Base#createActionItemConfig` accepts. `null` / `undefined` / `[]` all mean "no host actions for this node". |
| **lifecycle** | **Node-static.** Resolved per tabs node; the resulting action instances live for that node's retained lifetime and are **not** rebuilt on reprojection. Vary an action per active item by moving `hidden` / `disabled` on its stable instance — the mechanism `Workspace#syncDockCloseAction` already uses for the engine's own close action. |
| **re-resolution** | The resolver IS asked again when a commit re-projects a node — measured, not assumed. For a **retained** node the returned set is then **discarded**: the existing action instances win. So a resolver returning a different set on a later call has no effect, which is the mechanical reason `node-static` is a contract the machinery can actually keep rather than a convention. |
| ordering | Host actions project **before** the close action, so `close` keeps the rightmost position it already occupies for every consumer that enables it. |
| focus gating | Inherited from the tab header's `actionDefaults` (`showOnFocus: true`), so a host action is exposed with its TabContainer unless it opts out. No Dock-specific gating exists. |

### Name rules — enforced, not documented

| rule | behaviour |
|---|---|
| every host action carries a semantic `action` name | missing ⇒ **throws** at projection |
| names unique per tabs node | duplicate ⇒ **throws**, naming the action and the node |
| `close` reserved while `enableDockCloseAction` is on | ⇒ **throws**, naming the node |
| `close` usable when `enableDockCloseAction` is off | allowed — scoped rule, nothing to shadow |

Throwing rather than dropping is deliberate and matches `toolbar.Base#createActionItemConfig`, which
already throws for an unknown action and for an icon-only action with no accessible name. Names
*address* actions — `getActionItem(name)` returns the first match and intents route by name — so a
duplicate leaves one control permanently unreachable, and a host `close` projecting first would
capture both the engine's `hidden` policy sync and its close intent. Both failures are silent to a
host that only sees a header missing a control.

### Intent — the `dockHeaderAction` event

| aspect | contract |
|---|---|
| emitted by | `DockWorkspace#onDockHeaderAction`, for every action this class does not own |
| owned by the class | exactly `close`, and only while `enableDockCloseAction` is on; that one is routed through the model and is **not** re-emitted |
| payload | `{action, dockNodeId, tabContainer}` plus the emitter's own `source` (the workspace id), added by `fire` |
| return | `onDockHeaderAction` returns `null` for an unowned action — the workspace declines to act, it does not swallow |
| host requirement | none: listen on the workspace. No subclass and no protected-method override. |
| wiring | bound unconditionally, so a host projecting only its own actions — with the close action **off** — still receives intents. |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A Dock host can project additional actions into a tabs node's header without patching the
      adapter, using the documented projection-options hook.
- [ ] A host-authored action's intent reaches the host, with the tabs node identified — proven by an
      arm that fails if the listener still filters on `close`.
- [ ] Host actions compose with `enableDockCloseAction`: both present together, and either usable
      alone. In particular a host with custom actions and **no** close action still receives intents.
- [ ] Host actions are focus-gated by the tab-header default unless they opt out, with no
      Dock-specific gating code.
- [ ] Reconciliation keeps host actions stable across a re-projection — an action instance is not
      replaced on every commit, so `actionVisibilityChange` consumers such as tab Overflow keep
      working.

## Out of Scope

- The gating vocabulary itself — #17874 owns `showOnFocus`.
- Changing close-action semantics.
